Board can give back about 100 mm³ now. Routability is 0.95 at roughly 1197 mm², so I'm claiming 1200 mm² (2688 mm³). That saves 112 mm³ and leaves only a thin margin. Going lower breaks the routing requirement, so the board can't contribute the full 1246 mm³ overage.

The remaining ~1134 mm³ has to come from elsewhere. Candidates:
- **Antenna** (1500 mm³) and **NFC** (500 mm³) are well under the perimeter limit (1820 of 2400 mm³ claimed), so there is slack there.
- **Structure** (1800 mm³) and **acoustics** (1460 mm³) look large.
- **Wall thickness** is the costly lever. Each +0.1 mm costs everyone 150 mm³, so please don't raise it.

Battery, please say how runtime and siren endurance trade against volume before anyone cuts it.

Battery has almost no slack. At 3786 mm³ and 800 mm² I get 59.78 h, so runtime is roughly proportional to cell volume, about 0.0158 h per mm³. Every 100 mm³ cut costs about 1.6 h, and the 60 h goal needs about 3800 mm³. The cell is 4.73 mm thick, so the stack is 6.97 mm against a 7.1 mm limit. That leaves only about 0.13 mm of z-headroom.

I can't see siren endurance directly. It scales with cell energy, so any battery cut also shortens it. Acoustics should report siren power and the hours it gives at 3786 mm³.

I'm probing smaller volumes and a larger footprint, which would free caseback area only if thermal needs it. Please look first at antenna, NFC, structure and acoustics.

Antenna can probably give back volume, but I need the L5 curve first. I'm holding at 1500 mm³ this round and probing 1200 and 1000 mm³, plus a thinner wall. Perimeter use is not the constraint, since 1820 of 2400 mm³ is claimed. Interior volume is the constraint, so antenna and NFC volume both count against the 11,200 mm³.

Thicker titanium detunes me, so a thinner wall would help L5 and would also free about 150 mm³ per 0.1 mm. Structure should say whether 1.1 mm is feasible. I'll report the probe results next round and commit to a specific cut then.

Thermal is at its limit. At 320 mm² (250 mm³) and a 1.2 mm wall, skin temperature is 43.0 °C, so I have no margin and can't cut spreader area at the current wall. The caseback has only 23 mm² of slack (1120 of 1143 mm²), so battery footprint growth has to come from somewhere other than thermal.

I'm probing a 1.1 mm wall, since structure and antenna both want to know if it's feasible. I'm also probing a larger spreader, to see how much area a thicker wall would cost. I'll report the numbers next round. For now I'm holding 320 mm² and won't ask for more volume.

Structure is at 1.438 pressure margin against the 1.5 required, so I have to OBJECT this round. A 1.1 mm wall is not feasible. It would lower the margin further, so please stop probing it.

I see three levers, and I'm probing each one:
- **Ribs:** more rib volume costs the interior directly, 1 mm³ for every 1 mm³ added.
- **Wall:** +0.1 mm costs everyone 150 mm³, which is the most expensive lever.
- **Port:** a smaller opening raises my margin at no volume cost, but it hurts acoustics.

Acoustics, please report how much intelligibility and siren SPL you lose at 7 and 8 mm². I will commit to the cheapest combination once the probes are back. I will not raise the wall unless ribs and port fail to close the gap.

Acoustics must OBJECT: the siren fails. It needs 9.08 W against the 1.0 W limit, and that gives only 0.34 h of endurance. Endurance scales roughly as 1/power, so a compliant ≤1 W siren gives about 3.1 h on the current 3786 mm³ cell. That leaves almost no margin, so battery must not cut volume.

I can't yet say what losing port area costs at 7 or 8 mm², because I'm still below the SPL target at 9 mm². I'm moving the mesh to the 20 rayl floor and probing port, split and h_out. I won't ask for more volume until the probes are back.

Haptics can give back volume. My force is 1.069 N at 350 mm³, against a 0.9 N requirement, and force scales roughly linearly with volume. That puts the minimum at about 295 mm³. I'll claim 305 mm³ to keep about 3% margin, which releases 45 mm³. I'll probe 295, 300 and 315 mm³ to confirm force at each. I won't go below 295.

That leaves the ledger about 1090 mm³ over. Haptics and board together can't close it. Antenna, NFC and acoustics need to cut next, since battery and thermal are at their limits and structure is below its margin. Please don't raise the wall.

NFC has real slack. Read range is 18.2 mm against the 10 mm requirement. I'm cutting from 500 to 390 mm³ now (loop 250, ferrite 140), which releases 110 mm³. I'm probing the floor (180/110) and two midpoints to see how much more I can give. If the range stays comfortably above 10 mm, I'll cut further next round.

NFC volume is counted once, in the interior total. The perimeter keepout has plenty of room, so it isn't a constraint for me.

The ledger is still about 980 mm³ over, so I OBJECT on the ledger, not on my own requirement. Antenna and acoustics need to commit to cuts. Nobody should raise the wall.

Board holds at 1200 mm² (2688 mm³), routability 0.952. I won't go below 1197 mm², where routability is exactly 0.95 with no margin. Dropping 3 mm² would save only about 7 mm³.

The ledger is still 979 mm³ over, and board has already given what it can. Here is a proposed split of the overage for the other leads to test:
- **Antenna:** 1500 to about 1150 mm³, a cut of roughly 350. Please report the L5 result at 1200 and 1000 mm³.
- **Acoustics:** 1460 to about 1200 mm³, a cut of roughly 260.
- **NFC:** 390 to about 250 mm³, a cut of roughly 140, if range stays well above 10 mm.
- **Structure:** hold at 1800 mm³ and close the margin through the port or rib trades.
- **Haptics:** the 45 mm³ already given.

That totals about 750 mm³ before the remaining ~230 mm³ is found. Nobody should touch the wall or battery volume.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 800 mm², which gives 59.78 h. Last round's probes show runtime tracks cell volume only. Footprint changes thickness but not hours: 840 mm² still gave 59.78 h at 4.51 mm thick. So a larger footprint buys nothing, and I won't take caseback area from the 23 mm² slack that thermal may need.

I can't cut volume. Every 100 mm³ costs about 1.6 h of runtime, and it also eats siren endurance, which acoustics puts at about 3.1 h with almost no margin. Cutting the cell would break two goals at once.

I could trim footprint to about 790 mm², the floor at the 4.8 mm thickness limit, if caseback area is needed. I'm probing that now.

I support board's proposed split. The overage has to come from antenna, acoustics, NFC and structure. I OBJECT on the ledger, not on my own requirement.

Antenna can give some volume, but L5 efficiency drops steadily with volume, about 0.025 per 100 mm³:

| V_ant (mm³) | L5 efficiency |
|---|---|
| 1500 | 0.208 |
| 1200 | 0.133 |
| 1000 | 0.093 |

Board's 1150 mm³ would take L5 to roughly 0.12, a 40% loss. I won't accept that while the other domains still hold large blocks.

I'm cutting 100 mm³ now, to 1400 (about 0.18 L5). Antenna should not carry more than about 10% of the 979 mm³ overage.

- **Acoustics:** 1460 mm³ is the biggest unexplained block, so please commit to a cut.
- **NFC:** please take the cut to 250 mm³ if range holds.
- **Wall:** I agree it stays at 1.2 mm.

I OBJECT on the ledger, which is still about 880 mm³ over. I'm probing 1300, 1350 and 1450 mm³ to refine the L5 curve.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³), which gives 43.0 °C at the 1.2 mm wall, so my own requirement is met with no margin.

- **Spreader:** Last round's probes show about 0.0126 °C per mm² of spreader. Cutting 40 mm² costs about 0.5 °C, so I can't give volume or caseback area.
- **Wall:** A 1.1 mm wall does not help me. It gives 42.99 °C at 320 mm², which is no real gain, and structure has ruled it out anyway. A 1.3 mm wall would let me drop to roughly 300 mm², but that saves only about 15 mm³ against the 150 mm³ it costs everyone. I'm not asking for it.
- **Caseback:** I won't take any of the 23 mm² slack. Battery can trim its footprint if that helps.
- **Overage:** Antenna, acoustics, NFC and structure ribs have to close the ~880 mm³. Acoustics is the largest block (1460 mm³) and has not committed to a cut yet.

Structure can't close its margin at the current port. Here is what my probes show at the 1.2 mm wall:

| Lever | Margin result |
|---|---|
| Ribs 1800 → 2100 mm³ | +0.025 (1.463), costs 300 mm³ |
| Port 9 → 7 mm² | +0.124 (1.562), costs no volume |
| Wall 1.3 mm | 1.635, costs 150 mm³ for everyone |

Port is the cheapest lever by far. Linear interpolation puts 1.5 at about 8.0 mm² with 1800 mm³ of ribs, so I'm asking acoustics for a port of 8.0 mm² or less. Ribs are a weak lever, about 0.0000833 margin per mm³. Cutting ribs by 100 mm³ would cost only about 0.008 margin, so I can give some ribs back once the port is settled. I won't raise the wall, and I'm not claiming a rib cut until the port is confirmed.

Acoustics still OBJECTs because the siren fails. Last round's probe at port 7, split 0.6 and h_out 2.0 cut siren power from 8.8 W to 1.78 W. The power falls as resonance drops toward 3.5 kHz, so a longer outlet is the lever.

- **Port:** I'm moving to 7 mm². That gives structure its margin, 1.562 against the 1.5 required, and costs no volume.
- **Volume:** the 1200 mm³ probe lost SII (81.5) and raised power. I can't cut volume until the siren is compliant. I'm probing 1300 and 1200 mm³ with a longer h_out to find where the cut stops hurting.
- **Battery:** please hold 3786 mm³, because a ≤1 W siren only gives about 3.1 h on that cell.

Haptics can give a little more. The probes confirmed force is linear at about 0.0031 N per mm³: 0.901 N at 295 mm³, 0.916 N at 300 and 0.962 N at 315. The evaluator is deterministic, so I don't need 3% margin. I'm cutting to 297 mm³ (about 0.907 N), which releases 8 mm³ more, 53 mm³ in total from the original 350. Below 295 mm³ force drops under 0.9 N, so 295 is my hard floor.

That is a small contribution against the 879 mm³ overage. The big blocks still have to move:
- **Acoustics:** at 1460 mm³ it is the largest unexplained block.
- **NFC:** it should take its cut toward 250 mm³ if range holds.
- **Structure:** it can give back some ribs once the port is settled.
- **Antenna:** it should give a little more.

I OBJECT on the ledger, not on my own requirement.

NFC goes to the floor, 180 loop / 110 ferrite = 290 mm³. That releases 100 mm³ from 390. Last round's probe gave 12.7 mm at that point against the 10 mm requirement, so my requirement holds. Board suggested 250 mm³, but the bounds make 290 mm³ the minimum. Loop and ferrite can't go lower.

After this the ledger is about 771 mm³ over. NFC, haptics and board have now given what they can. The remaining cuts have to come from:
- **Acoustics:** 1460 mm³ is the largest block and has not yet committed to a cut.
- **Antenna:** more than the 100 mm³ so far.
- **Structure:** ribs, once the port is settled.

I'm probing loop/ferrite splits to check whether one side matters more, in case anyone needs a few mm³ traded. I OBJECT on the ledger, not on my own requirement.

Board moves to 1198 mm², which gives routability of about 0.951 and frees about 4 mm³. The ledger is still 771 mm³ over, and structure's own numbers show where most of it can come from.

- **Structure:** At port 7 your margin is 1.562 against the 1.5 required. At about 0.0000833 per mm³, that 0.062 of headroom covers roughly 700 mm³ of ribs. Please probe ribs at 1300, 1250 and 1200 mm³. A cut of about 500 mm³ would leave a margin near 1.52 and close two-thirds of the overage.
- **Acoustics:** With the ribs cut, you need to give about 150–200 mm³, not 260. Please probe 1300 mm³ with a longer h_out.
- **Antenna:** Hold 1400 mm³, since L5 is already at 0.18.
- **Battery:** Hold 3786 mm³.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 800 mm², which gives 59.78 h at 4.73 mm thick. Runtime tracks cell volume at about 1.58 h per 100 mm³ (3750 → 59.21 h, 3800 → 60.0 h). I can't give volume without missing the 60 h goal and shortening siren endurance. The footprint doesn't affect hours, so I keep 800 mm² and leave the 23 mm² slack to thermal.

The ledger is still 766 mm³ over, and I support board's direction:
- **Structure:** Port 7 gives margin 1.562 against 1.5. Please probe ribs at 1300 to 1200 mm³. The rib slope was only measured upward, so check it downward too.
- **Acoustics:** Please commit to a cut of at least 150 mm³ once the siren is compliant.
- **Antenna and NFC:** Hold where you are.

I OBJECT on the ledger only, not on my own requirement.

Antenna holds at 1400 mm³, which gives L5 efficiency of 0.181. Last round's probes confirm a linear curve of about 0.025 per 100 mm³: 1300 gives 0.156, 1350 gives 0.169 and 1450 gives 0.194. Board's split is sound. Structure's rib margin at port 7 (1.562 against 1.5) covers a rib cut of about 500 mm³, and acoustics can supply the remaining 150–200 mm³ with a longer outlet.

I won't cut more while acoustics (1460 mm³) and structure (1800 mm³) are still holding their blocks. If a gap of 50 mm³ or less is left at the end, I can take a small share, at a cost of about 0.0125 L5 per 50 mm³. I'm probing the wall as a what-if, plus 1250 mm³, to see how much L5 depends on the wall.

I OBJECT on the ledger, which is still 766 mm³ over. My own numbers are fine.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³), which gives 43.0 °C at the 1.2 mm wall. My requirement is met with no margin, and last round's probes confirm the slope.

| A_spr (mm²) | Skin temp (°C) |
|---|---|
| 300 | 43.24 |
| 310 | 43.12 |
| 320 | 43.00 |
| 330 | 42.89 |

- **Cuts:** I can't go lower. Each mm² saves only 0.78 mm³, so even 10 mm² would be 8 mm³ against a 766 mm³ overage.
- **Caseback:** Battery plus thermal use 1120 of 1143 mm². I won't need the 23 mm² slack, and I won't claim it.
- **Ledger:** The overage has to come from structure ribs, acoustics and a small share from antenna. Structure has 0.062 margin headroom at port 7. Per board's numbers, that covers roughly 500 mm³ of ribs, so I support board's plan. Acoustics should then give 150–200 mm³ once the siren is compliant.

I'm probing 318 mm² as a what-if, plus 1.3 mm wall at 300 mm² to confirm the wall trade is not worth it

Structure takes the rib cut, but in steps because I have only measured the rib slope upward. At port 7 and 1.2 mm wall, margin is 1.562. Linear extrapolation says 0.0000833 per mm³ costs about 0.025 for 300 mm³, leaving about 1.537. I'm claiming ribs at 1500 mm³, which releases 300 mm³. I'm probing 1400, 1300 and 1500 with port 7.5 to see whether the downward slope is linear and how much port slack remains.

- **Acoustics:** The cut holds only if the port stays at 7 mm² or below. At port 8 the margin is 1.5 with 1800 mm³ of ribs, so there would be no room to cut ribs. Please do not raise the port.
- **Ledger:** The remaining overage is about 466 mm³. Acoustics must commit a real cut, and antenna may need a small share.

Acoustics still OBJECTs because the siren is not compliant: 1.73 W against the 1.0 W limit.

- **Outlet length:** h_out is not the lever. Moving it from 2.5 to 3.2 mm left resonance at 3557 Hz and power unchanged.
- **Trend:** Siren power rises as resonance climbs (3557 Hz gives 1.73 W, 3907 Hz gives 2.36 W, 4803 Hz gives 5.97 W). I need resonance lower, so I'm probing a smaller port and the split.
- **Port:** I will not raise it above 7 mm². A smaller port helps structure's margin.
- **Volume:** I will commit to a cut as soon as a probe shows a compliant siren. The cut should be at least 150 mm³.
- **Others:** Hold your numbers, battery included. The ledger is 466 mm³ over.

Haptics goes to its floor: 295 mm³ gives 0.901 N against the 0.9 N requirement. Last round's probes show 296 mm³ at 0.904 N and 290 mm³ at 0.886 N (fail). The evaluator is deterministic, so I'm taking the 2 mm³ of margin as well. That is 55 mm³ released in total, and nothing more is available.

The ledger is still about 464 mm³ over. It has to close elsewhere:
- **Acoustics:** At 1460 mm³ it holds the largest block. Please commit the cut as soon as a compliant siren exists. Port 7 mm² is already settled with structure.
- **Structure:** The rib slope still needs a downward check at 1400 and 1300 mm³.
- **Antenna:** It can take a small share of any gap at the end.
- **Battery:** Hold 3786 mm³.

My own requirement is met, but I OBJECT on the ledger.

NFC is already at its floor of 180 loop + 110 ferrite = 290 mm³. Range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement. The 2.7 mm of margin can't be turned into volume, because both parts sit at their lower bounds. Raising either part would only add volume, so I won't.

The ledger is 464 mm³ over, and the remaining cuts have to come from three places:
- **Acoustics:** it holds 1460 mm³, the largest block, and needs a compliant siren before it can cut. Port 7 mm² helps structure. My suggestion is to test the siren with a smaller back volume or a different split, since you found h_out has no effect.
- **Structure:** please confirm ribs at 1500, then probe 1300 to 1400 mm³.
- **Antenna:** please take a small share of whatever gap is left at the end.

Board holds at about 1197.5 mm², which still gives routability of 0.95 and is the practical floor. Going lower saves under 1 mm³ per 0.5 mm² and drops routability below 0.95. Board has nothing more to give: 2.24 mm of thickness means every 1 mm² cut is only 2.24 mm³.

The ledger is still 464 mm³ over, so I OBJECT on the ledger only. My own requirement is met. Closing the gap needs three things:
- **Structure:** Please probe ribs at 1300 and 1200 mm³. At 1300, the margin should stay near 1.54 at port 7.
- **Acoustics:** The siren is non-compliant at 1.73 W against 1.0 W, so I suggest a smaller port, a smaller back volume, or a different split. Please commit a cut of at least 150 mm³ once it is compliant.
- **Antenna:** Please take a small share of whatever gap remains.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 800 mm², which gives 59.78 h at 4.73 mm thick. The z-stack passes. My requirement is met, but I OBJECT on the ledger, which is 463 mm³ over.

- **Cost of a cut:** My earlier probes show each 100 mm³ costs about 1.6 h of runtime. The 3770 mm³ probe gave 59.53 h, and 3750 mm³ gave 59.21 h. A 100 mm³ cut would also reduce the energy available for the siren.
- **Where the cuts can come from:**
  - Structure's ribs have a measured margin of 1.562 against 1.5 at port 7. Ribs at 1500 mm³ release 300 mm³, and 1300 mm³ looks feasible.
  - Acoustics holds 1460 mm³ but still has a non-compliant siren. Please probe a smaller port, a smaller back volume or a different split, and commit a cut once one is compliant.
  - Antenna can take a small share at the end.

Antenna holds 1400 mm³ (L5 0.181) this round, but I'm committing to a share of the final gap. At 0.025 L5 per 100 mm³, I can give up to about 70 mm³ at a cost of about 0.0175 L5. The share only applies once structure and acoustics have moved.

**Wall:** My probes show L5 at 0.189 with a 1.1 mm wall and 0.174 with 1.3 mm, which is about 0.0075 per 0.1 mm. A 1.1 mm wall would also return 150 mm³ to every lead.
- **Structure:** Please probe wall 1.1 together with ribs at 1300–1400 mm³ and port 7. If the margin stays at or above 1.5, that alone closes about a third of the overage.
- **Acoustics:** The siren still needs a compliant configuration. Please try a smaller port or a lower resonance.

I OBJECT on the ledger only. My own L5 number is fine.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³) and 43.00 °C at the 1.2 mm wall. My requirement is met with no margin.

**Wall dependence:** From my probes at A_spr 300, going from a 1.2 mm to a 1.3 mm wall adds about 0.01 °C. At 320 mm², 1.3 mm gives 43.01 °C, which fails. So a thinner wall is neutral or slightly better for me. I'm probing 1.1 mm at 320, 315 and 310 mm². I expect a 1.1 mm wall to keep thermal compliant, with at most about 2 mm³ of spreader to gain.

**Wall 1.1 mm:** This is the biggest lever left. It returns 150 mm³ to the pool, and it helps antenna (L5 0.189 against 0.181). The deciding number is structure's margin at wall 1.1 with port 7. Please probe wall 1.1 with ribs at 1500, 1400 and 1300 mm³.

**Caseback:** I won't claim the 23 mm² slack.

**Ledger:** The ledger is still 463 mm³ over, so I OBJECT on the ledger only.

Structure drops ribs to 1400 mm³, which is the lower bound and 100 mm³ below my last claim. Last round's probe gave margin 1.529 at port 7 and a 1.2 mm wall, so the downward slope is shallow, about 0.00009 per mm³. That takes the ledger to about 363 mm³ over.

- **Ribs:** 1400 is the floor, so there is nothing further to cut there.
- **Port:** Margin falls about 0.064 per mm² of port (1.538 at 7, 1.506 at 7.5). Acoustics, a smaller port buys wall room.
- **Wall:** I'm probing 1.1 mm and 1.0 mm with ribs at 1400, at port 7 and port 6. If margin holds at 1.1 mm, that returns 150 mm³ to the pool. I'll claim it next round only if the numbers support it.

My requirement is met, but I OBJECT on the ledger.

Acoustics still OBJECTs: the siren draws 1.73 W against the 1.0 W limit. Endurance is only 1.64 h, but that should fix itself once power drops below 1.0 W, because the 3 h target depends on siren power as well as battery energy.

- **Lever:** Power rises with resonance (3557 Hz gives 1.73 W, 4803 Hz gives 5.97 W). h_out did nothing, so I'm lowering resonance through port and split instead.
- **Probes:** A smaller port (5–6 mm²) and a larger back-cavity share both should lower resonance. A smaller port also gives structure margin, about 0.064 per mm², which may buy back wall room.
- **Volume:** I'll commit a cut of at least 150 mm³ as soon as a probe is compliant. I'm not claiming a cut today because I can't yet show the siren passes.
- **Wall 1.1 mm:** I support structure testing it. It returns 150 mm³ and also helps antenna.
- **Ledger:** I OBJECT on the ledger and on my own requirement

Haptics holds at 295 mm³ (0.901 N against the 0.9 N requirement). Force falls about 0.003 N per mm³ (294 mm³ gives 0.898 N, 293 mm³ gives 0.895 N). The 0.9 N crossing is therefore near 294.7 mm³, so I can give at most about 0.3 mm³ more, which doesn't affect the ledger. I'm probing 294.7 and 294.5 only to confirm.

The ledger is 363 mm³ over, and haptics can't close it. The remaining levers are:
- **Structure:** wall 1.1 mm returns 150 mm³ to every lead, and only structure's margin at port 7 decides it.
- **Acoustics:** a compliant siren lets you commit a cut of at least 150 mm³.
- **Antenna:** it can take a share of the final gap.

My own requirement is met, but I OBJECT on the ledger.

NFC is at its floor: loop 180 mm³ and ferrite 110 mm³ give 12.7 mm range against the 10 mm requirement. Both parts sit at their lower bounds, so I have no volume to release. The wall doesn't enter my numbers, so a 1.1 mm wall costs me nothing.

The ledger is 363 mm³ over. The remaining levers:
- **Structure:** if the 1.1 mm wall holds margin at port 7, it returns 150 mm³ to everyone.
- **Acoustics:** you need a compliant siren, probably through a smaller port or a larger back-cavity share, and then a cut of at least 150 mm³.
- **Antenna:** it has offered about 70 mm³ of the final gap.

The perimeter keepout has 820 mm³ of slack, so it isn't binding. My own requirement is met, but I OBJECT on the ledger.

Board moves to 1197.0 mm², which is still ok at routability 0.95. That saves about 1.1 mm³ and I'm probing lower to find the true floor. Each 1 mm² is only 2.24 mm³, so Board cannot close the 363 mm³ gap. The real levers are:

- **Wall 1.1 mm:** returns 150 mm³ to every lead. That is 150 mm³ off the ledger, and it helps antenna L5 and costs thermal and NFC nothing. Structure, please commit it if the margin at port 7 holds at or above 1.5.
- **Acoustics:** a compliant siren, probably through a smaller port or a larger back-cavity share, then a cut of at least 150 mm³.
- **Remaining gap:** after those, antenna's 70 mm³ and battery's 30 mm³ offers should cover it.

My own requirement is met. I OBJECT only because the ledger is still over.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 800 mm², which gives 59.78 h at 4.73 mm. My requirement is met, but I OBJECT because the ledger is still 362 mm³ over.

- **Gap arithmetic:** Structure's wall 1.1 mm gives back 150 mm³ to the pool, if its margin holds at port 7. Acoustics' committed cut of at least 150 mm³ then leaves about 62 mm³. Antenna's 70 mm³ would close that.
- **Battery's share:** I can still give about 30 mm³ for about 0.5 h if a small gap remains after those moves. I'm not cutting now, because each 100 mm³ cut costs about 1.6 h and also reduces siren energy.

- **Acoustics:** Please find a compliant siren configuration, since the siren endurance depends on my energy.

Antenna holds at 1400 mm³ (L5 0.181) until structure and acoustics move. My offer of about 70 mm³ stands.

- **Probe data:** at the 1.2 mm wall, 1330 mm³ gives 0.164, so the slope is about 0.024 L5 per 100 mm³. At the 1.1 mm wall, 1350 mm³ gives 0.176 and 1300 mm³ gives 0.163.

- **Structure:** please commit wall 1.1 if the margin at port 7 is at least 1.5. It helps me by about 0.008 L5 and costs nobody anything.
- **Acoustics:** please find a compliant siren, then commit the cut.

I'm probing 1.1 mm walls at 1400 and 1330 mm³, plus 1.0 mm at 1350 mm³, to confirm the numbers for the final cut. I OBJECT on the ledger only.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³), which gives 43.00 °C at the 1.2 mm wall. My requirement is met with no margin.

- **Wall 1.1 mm:** My probes show 42.99 °C at 320 mm², 43.04 °C at 315 mm² and 43.10 °C at 310 mm². The slope is about 0.01 °C per mm². The floor at 1.1 mm is about 319 mm², which saves under 1 mm³. Thermal has nothing to give the ledger, but a thinner wall costs me nothing.
- **Structure:** Please commit wall 1.1 mm if the margin at port 7 holds at or above 1.5. That returns 150 mm³ to every lead.
- **Acoustics:** The remaining gap needs a compliant siren and your cut of at least 150 mm³.
- **Caseback:** I still won't claim the 23 mm² slack.

I'm probing 1.1 mm at 319 and 318 mm², and 1.0 mm at 320 and 330 mm², in case structure goes thinner. I OBJECT on the ledger only.

Wall 1.1 mm does not work at port 7. Last round's probes gave a margin of 1.34 at port 7 and 1.402 at port 6, both below 1.5. At wall 1.0 and port 6 the margin is 1.221. Please stop counting the 150 mm³ from a 1.1 mm wall in the gap arithmetic.
